⚔️The Next Room - Every room is a test.

🚪Every door hides a new nightmare. Every room could be your last.

⚠️WARNING: This game contains flashing lights, intense combat, and fast-paced action that may not be suitable for players with photosensitive epilepsy.

The Next Room is a fast-paced 3D action roguelite where every room is a new challenge and every decision can mean the difference between survival and death. Fight your way through relentless monsters, avoid deadly traps, uncover hidden secrets, and defeat powerful bosses guarding the path ahead.

No two runs are the same. Experiment with different builds, discover rare equipment, craft stronger gear, and adapt your strategy as you venture deeper into the unknown. Will you spend your hard-earned gold in the shop, search for hidden rooms, or save your resources for the battles yet to come? Only those who keep moving will discover what lies behind... the next room.

🎯Gameplay Features

🤺Battle through rooms filled with dangerous enemies.

👹Face challenging bosses with unique abilities and attack patterns.

🛠️Craft and upgrade your equipment to create powerful builds.

🎭Customize your character to match your preferred playstyle.

🪤Survive deadly traps scattered throughout the dungeon.

🛒Discover and visit the shop to buy valuable items and upgrades.

🔐Discover secret rooms containing rare rewards and hidden surprises.

🎒Item system:

  • Single-Use Items – powerful effects for critical moments.

  • Run Items – temporary buffs lasting until death.

  • Permanent Upgrades – long-term progression across all runs.

🔄️Highly replayable runs with randomized layouts, enemies, and builds.

THE NIGHT KITCHEN

You just started a new job. You're standing in a kitchen. Grill, oven, coffee machine. Take orders, prepare food, hand it to the customer. Simple work

Each night is stranger than the last. The customers keep coming back. Their words don't fit this place. Or you. Or maybe they fit a little too well?

The kitchen never sleeps. And neither should you.

The longer you're here, the more you understand. But you're just not sure you want to. 

Features

  • 7 nights - each one brings new customers, new equipment, and new tasks

  • Growing kitchen - grill, oven, deep fryer, coffee machine. With every night, you have more tools and more to cook

  • Familiar customers - the same customers return. And each time, they know a little more about you

This is an incredibly smooth 3D roguelike.

If you're looking for fast-paced, satisfying roguelike gameplay, this game is well worth a try.

 🐾 Core Gameplay

Do whatever it takes to dodge enemy attacks while following the arrows to find and collect equipment.

Once you've picked up an item, open the Equipment Panel and add it to the appropriate slot.

Item Colors：

🟢 Green — Weapons

🟡 Yellow — Weapon Upgrades

🔴 Red — Stat Upgrades

 🐾 Story

The protagonist is a cat named A-Jiu.

As time and space fall into chaos, fragments of countless past cycles begin to flood into the chaotic Ninth Cycle.

Toys that once kept A-Jiu company,

objects filled with precious memories,

have taken on new forms.

Some have become terrifying enemies.

Others have awakened as sentient weapons.

🐾 Automated Systems

Auto Pickup:

Automatically pick up items when you get close to them.

Auto Attack:

Nearby enemies are automatically locked onto and attacked.

The next signal could change everything.

The Nugget is a first-person gold-prospecting simulation set in the Australian outback. Pack your tools, plan your supplies and explore promising ground. Your finds fund better equipment and your next expedition.

Learn the signal

Sweep the ground with different detectors and settings. Narrow down a signal, dig with your tools and recover the target. Not every signal means gold: decide which patch deserves more work.

Work the dirt

Collect promising material and wash out the gold. Set up processing equipment and connect the water and power it needs. More capacity only helps when you can supply your operation.

Build a working camp

Build your camp freely with foundations, walls, doors, roofs and fences. Set up a place to sleep, light a fire, cook food and connect power sources to your machines. Keep food, water and fuel ready for your next trip.

Turn finds into a future

Sell gold, cover running costs and invest in better tools. Carefully search a patch for individual nuggets or prepare a longer expedition. Account for the weather and return with knowledge as well as gold.

The Observation Exit is a first-person psychological horror game where you identify anomalies to escape an endless hospital corridor. Observe strange changes, survive deadly entities, and find the correct path forward!

Explore an endless hospital corridor filled with subtle anomalies and constantly shifting details. Trapped in a repeating loop, every elevator leads you back to the same place. As you move forward, the once-familiar corridor begins to feel increasingly wrong.

CAPTURE ANOMALIES

Break the loop by relying on your memory and attention to detail. Observe the corridor carefully and identify any unusual changes before reaching the elevator. Missing or misjudging an anomaly will reset your progress. Make the right decisions consistently to move forward and escape. Successfully progress through 10 levels to escape.

CHOOSE THE CORRECT ELEVATOR

Progress by choosing the correct elevator at the end of each corridor. If everything appears normal, take the left path forward. Selecting the wrong option will send you back or worsen the loop. Consistent, correct choices are the only way to advance.

AVOID EACH ENTITY

Watch out for what’s hiding in the corridor. Staying too long or making mistakes can draw unwanted attention. Use your awareness, movement, and timing to avoid each entity, as they appear suddenly and react differently to your actions.

Experience a grounded, realistic environment with minimal UI and a focus on immersion. The hospital feels quiet, sterile, and unsettling, creating a constant sense of tension as you move through the corridor.

FEATURES:

• Explore a looping hospital corridor that changes over time.

• Identify a wide range of anomalies, from obvious to extremely subtle.

• Make decisions at each elevator to determine your progression.

• Face entities that react to your mistakes and behavior.

• Rely on memory and attention to detail to survive.

• Short, tense, and replayable psychological horror experience.

Pick up words (#Word) from conversations and customers’ belongings to get to the bottom of the truth.

In this game, you take on the role of a former detective and unravel the mystery behind an incident that unfolds in a quiet coffee shop.

🔍 Extract [#Word] from customers’ conversations and the shop interior

Suspicious statements exchanged by customers across the counter, and a sense of unease lingering in the quiet shop. Find the keywords (#Word) hidden within the text and record them in your detective notebook.

🧩 [Deduction Slots] that rearrange your thoughts

Fit the words (#Word) you’ve gathered into the deduction slots to construct the sentence of truth. It’s up to the player’s keen observational skills to connect the dots and expose the customers’ hidden “lies” and contradictions.

👁️ [Trauma] Lurking in a Black-and-White World

Every time you solve a case, memories of a “past fire” that scorch your mind intertwine in an unsettling way.

A burning building.

Blood-stained hands.

And questions about yourself.

The incidents that unfold at the café and the protagonist’s own past.

When all the mysteries converge, what truth awaits you in the end—?

Can you sharpen your observational skills (3D Investigation) and, within this world that’s turning monochrome, uncover “the greatest mystery of all: yourself”?

🪧 Game Features

  • Word-linking deduction puzzles: A challenging deduction system where you build logical chains using collected words, rather than simply choosing from options.

  • A 3D visual experience: A unique atmosphere of suspense created by the retro, cozy café setting and the observation mode (black-and-white).

  • Deepening psychological horror: A psychological horror narrative that gradually takes over the routine operations of a café.

The hotel is closed for the winter. You have the keys.

A seaside hotel on a coast nobody visits between October and March. The owner is away until spring. Her rules are pinned beside the key board in her own handwriting: No guests. I mean it this time. Boiler on at four, not before. The season still has an instalment to make and the boiler eats oil.

Somebody knocks.

After the last bus, in the rain, with cash and no booking, and a reason they would rather not give. Nobody comes to this coast in winter without one. You can ask, but you are a stranger behind a desk at night, and every question you ask tells them what you wanted to know.

Four answers at the desk

  • Give a key. They are in the house tonight. Their money is in the box, and so is whatever came with them.
  • Refuse. The last bus has gone. Refusing costs something, sometimes before morning.
  • Give a particular room. The one that matters.
  • Take the money and leave the night out of the book. The cash is yours, not the house's, and the register never says they were here.

The rooms are not interchangeable, and the house teaches you that slowly.

3 looks over the road: you can see who arrives, and so can they. 7 and 8 share a wall, so whoever sleeps in them hears each other. 12 is the only room with a line out. 19 is top floor, at the end, where nobody hears anything at all. A refusal is one bit of information. A room is a sentence: the man who asked about the road went in 19, and the woman who kept looking at the door went in 12, so she could call someone.

A full house is bad.

You cannot take every night's money and keep the house quiet. The more a stranger pays, the more it is worth asking why. The rules beside the key board were written by someone who will not be here in February.

Room 24

Pages are missing from the book on the desk. The town's list and the register disagree about who was here last winter, and the disagreement is legible if you keep both. The board still has the key to 24, the previous caretaker's room. You can open it on the first night. What is in there does not stop the season; it changes how you read every knock after it.

The season

  • A season of nights: arrivals, rooms, money, and the morning the ledger closes.
  • A hotel you walk in first person: the desk, the corridor, the rooms you let.
  • Guests stay. A key given is a key out; the board fills up, and the quiet room may already be holding someone.
  • Consequences arrive late, and they come back at the house.
  • A thread you assemble from the register, the town's list, and the room nobody has opened since last winter.
  • One season, one thread. It closes the way it was always going to; what changes is the last page of the register, who wrote it and what they left out.
  • No death and no failure that erases a run. The season can end with a room you never opened.

The Off-Season's scene art, character art, music and most sound effects are pre-generated with AI tools and then curated and edited by the developer; the remaining cues are synthesized by code. Its narrative text is human–AI co-written and human-edited under the author's direction. Nothing is generated while you play.

Hold the mouse over the crowd and the shrine's arms pull creatures to the altar. Every delivery pays Flame, and a streak of them pays more. There's no offline progress, so every number that goes up is one you pushed.

Flame buys faster arms, more arms, richer creatures and longer streaks. New cards unlock as the shrine grows. Catch a goblin for a short boost.

When night falls, enemies come out of the dark and you hold the mouse to fire. Kills earn boons, duplicates stack, and the deeper you get, the more shards you take home.

Spend your Shards on a skill tree full of permanent upgrades that make your days stronger.

Max out the Forest and ascend to the Desert, the Ocean and the Ice. Every world brings new creatures and bigger numbers, and each time you move on you choose one of three artifacts to keep for the rest of the run. The demo includes all four worlds.

In the beginning, it was a sacrifice. Now it is a spectacle. One gate, and only one side walks out.

Gods and demons fill the stands. You are the Sacrificer.

Summon monsters, outlast cunning hero bosses, and when the moment comes, offer three of your own and step onto the sand as the demon they worship. Every second you spend is a second of your life.

TIME IS YOUR LIFE

Time is the only currency. Summons, spells, upgrades and merchant deals all burn seconds.

Even opening your grimoire to think costs one.

Wound the heroes and the crowd throws you time. Stall too long and the Hour Moon wanes faster.

Hit zero, and the altar claims you and your whole army.

COMMAND THE LEGION

96 monsters across 9 races: skeletons, demons, hellspawn, nether, dragonkin, savages, wolves, spiders and beasts.

They fight on their own; you call the shots. But only six seals hold the field, so every summon is a choice.

Stack race synergies, fuse two monsters into a higher tier, feed the weak to the strong, and carry traits like lifesteal and resurrection through the run.

Some monsters mutate. The game won't point them out.

SACRIFICE THREE. BECOME THE DEMON.

Let enough of one race fall in the arena, offer three of your own monsters and five minutes of your life, and descend as their Avatar.

Switch from commander to real-time WASD action, mid-battle.

6 Avatars, from a blood-cursed wolf to a dragon of the void, each with four skills and a finisher of its own.

THE HEROES ARE THE BOSSES

10 heroes, each with their own AI. They dodge, flank, heal each other and punish your openings.

They level up and grow stronger the longer you stall. Kill them before they outgrow you.

And they don't come alone: their soldiers march in waves, raiders crash in to fight you both, and sometimes a Viking Giant walks through the gate.

DARK RITES & BLOOD BARGAINS

10 dark rites for when you'd rather do the killing yourself:

Soul Volley, Evil Whisper, Time Freeze... and a rain of Cute Slimes.

53 merchants come knocking, and they know how your run is going. One shows up when you're about to die. One smells your desperation and lends you time, at a price. One wants to buy your monsters.

Trade what's left of your life for monsters, traits, Blood Scrolls and 21 relics.

ONE LIFE. FIVE ARENAS.

Fight through five arenas on a single life.

No second is wasted: the time you survive is banked as Emberhours.

Spend it at the Ember Altar on permanent upgrades, and seal Blood Pacts to unlock new Avatars.

A Bestiary of 96 monsters, 30 achievements, and an ending worth reaching. Fully playable in 11 languages.

FREE DEMO

The first two arenas and three Avatars are free to play. See how long you last.

The Order Of Serenity is a psychological horror simulation where devotion, routine, and obedience shape your fate. You play as a young investigative journalist who infiltrates a secret cult to uncover the truth behind its practices. You are not a hero. You are an observer forced to become a participant.

Under the guise of a new recruit, you must blend in, follow orders, and avoid suspicion. Each day, the Order assigns you tasks. At first, they seem ordinary and harmless. Over time, these duties grow more disturbing, blurring the line between investigation and indoctrination.

The game focuses on atmosphere, tension, and moral discomfort rather than combat. Through repetitive rituals, strict schedules, and subtle psychological pressure, The Order Of Serenity explores how control is established and how obedience slowly replaces doubt.


As you rise through the ranks, you gain access to restricted areas, confidential information, and the inner circle of the cult. Your investigation deepens, but so does the risk. Every action is monitored. Every choice can either bring you closer to the truth or expose your true intentions.

Your goal is to uncover the secrets of the Order without losing yourself in the process.

Key Features

• Psychological horror driven by atmosphere and moral tension

• Narrative focused on infiltration and investigation

• Daily task based gameplay inspired by cult routines and control systems

• Rank and hierarchy progression within the Order

• Player choices that affect trust, access, and outcomes

• Minimalist mechanics designed to create unease and immersion

• Single player experience with a slow, oppressive pacing

You are the new ranger at a national park where tourist season is going almost according to plan.

By day, check documents, inspect vehicles, and let visitors into the park. By night, patrol the woods, help your fellow rangers, investigate strange incidents, and find out why something ancient, hungry, and definitely not approved by management is so desperate to get out.

Survive a Bureaucratic Nightmare

Fill out forms, bury inconvenient details, and try to explain to management why “ritual markings near the restroom” should not be listed as a standard maintenance issue.

Explore the Park on Foot, by Car, or by Boat

Reach the remote areas of Hampton Bay and keep an eye on your vehicle. A breakdown at the wrong time can leave you stranded far from your post.

Face the Horrors of Hampton Bay

Cultists, strange rituals, mutating people, and tourists who came back from the woods as something less than human will slowly become part of your shift.

Try to Hide the Evidence

Traces of incidents can be cleaned up, hidden, or left exactly where they are. Tourists, the police, and the detective will notice your choices.

Plan Each Day

Your energy is limited: work, running, driving, and night patrols all wear you down. Choose between your duties, the investigation, and your own safety.

A bookshop is a building full of strangers' lives.

You never met Arthur Pell. The solicitor's letter named you — Iris Calloway, of an address he had no reason to know — the will was in order, and the keys work. Above the door, in flaking gold: HERITAGE & SONS, and nobody left alive remembers any sons. Inside: his coat on the hook, his lamp on the counter, a ledger that stops mid-word — and shelving rules too strange to be housekeeping. The Baedeker is never shelved beside the atlases.

Every book here carries its previous owner.

Pressed violets from a garden that flowered at night. Love letters conducted entirely in the margins of second-hand novels. A soldier's promise folded into a book that outlived both parties. Buy and sell them, find the book each customer is really asking for, and keep the shop alive through the autumn of 1994.

And in the margins, one hand keeps recurring.

The inks age. The handwriting never does. It signs itself only "M." Pell spent years tracking it through his stock; his prices are still in the stock book under the counter, exactly where he left them, and the last thing he wrote was addressed to you: shelve by the rules, and do not read the margins.

How much you read is up to you. It always was.

What's inside

  • Keep the shop — buy collections, price finds, match books to the people who need them.
  • Read the owners — marginalia, inscriptions, photographs and pressed things, drawn from five decades of previous owners.
  • Follow what he left — the previous owner's prices in the stock book, his house rules, his errands, and the neighbours who still remember him.
  • Choose what the collection becomes — what you keep, what you release, and how close you let the hand in the margins come. Four endings.
  • Painted London, 1994; rain on the glass, lamplight in the aisles — and the back rows, where the bulbs keep dying.

Thrust Into Power

The former president is dead, and his place falls to you.

All you have to do, it seems, is keep the country running—

yet no document is ever trivial, and no signature comes without a price.

Insider Trading

You always know before the market does.

Because, after all, the news breaks at your desk.

Someone Always Loses

Your family, your people, and those not yet born.

Everyone is counting on you — but you can't answer them all.

No Way Out

A crisis no one can escape is closing in.

And when it comes—how will you be remembered?

## ABOUT THE QUEENS

The Queens is a fast-paced card, attention, and reflex game where 2–4 players face off around a single deck of cards. You can learn the rules in a few minutes; however, tracking the right card, reading your opponents' behavior, and choosing the perfect moment to play requires true mastery.

Each match begins with a standard 52-card deck. Cards are distributed as evenly as possible among the players, and everyone keeps their own deck face down. When it's their turn, players reveal the top card of their deck. As cards continue to accumulate in the center of the table, the next player is the one on the right.

The goal isn't just to play cards: when a valid combination forms in the center, you must act before the other players, win all the cards on the table, and add them to your own deck.

## FACE CARD CHALLENGES

When a Jack, Queen, King, or Ace is played, the normal round flow is interrupted, and a challenge begins. The next player has a limited number of attempts to reveal another face card:

- Ace: 1 attempt

- Jack: 2 attempts

- King: 3 attempts

- Queen: 4 attempts

If the responding player reveals another face card within their allotted attempts, the challenge does not end. The newly played face card sets a new challenge, and the task of responding passes to the next player.

For example, if a player plays a King, the next player has three attempts. If this player reveals a Queen on their second attempt, the challenge continues, and the next player now has four attempts.

If a player uses all their attempts but cannot reveal another face card, the owner of the last face card that initiated the challenge wins all the cards in the pot. Therefore, playing a strong face card can provide a great advantage; however, all plans can suddenly change when a valid hitting combination occurs on the table.

## WHEN CAN YOU HIT THE POT?

In The Queens, there are initially two basic hitting combinations:

- Double: Two consecutive cards of the same value appearing on the table. For example, two 7s, two Kings, or two Aces.

- Tost: The last card played and the two cards before it are of the same value. For example, 8–Jack–8 or Queen–3–Queen.

The suits and symbols of the cards are irrelevant; combinations are calculated based on the values ​​of the cards.

When a valid Double or Tost occurs, all living players can hit the table without waiting for their normal turn. Even if the Face Card Challenge is still active, the player who first notices the valid combination can hit the table.

The player who makes the first successful hit in the valid combination wins all the cards on the table. If more than one player attempts to hit simultaneously, the first valid hit confirmed by the server wins. Other players do not receive penalties for incorrect hits as they are attempting to hit within the valid window.

## THE PRICE OF A MISHIT

Speed ​​is important, but reckless play is dangerous. Hitting when there isn't a Double or Tost on the table is considered a mishit.

When a player with cards in their deck hits a mishit, they give a maximum of two cards from their deck as a penalty to the next active player. These cards can strengthen your opponent's deck and instantly change the balance of the match.

Therefore, you should not only strive to be faster than your opponents, but also ensure that the combination is truly valid. Sometimes hesitating costs you cards on the table; sometimes rushing gives your opponent free cards.

## EVEN IF YOU RUN OUT OF CARDS, IT'S NOT OVER

In three- or four-player matches, losing all the cards in your deck doesn't always mean you're instantly eliminated. A player who runs out of cards cannot play a card during their normal turn and is skipped during the round; however, they can continue to follow the table and hit valid combinations.

Each player has three lives for this comeback period.

If you hit a valid Double or Tost before anyone else when you have no cards left, you win all the cards in the pot and rejoin the game. Thus, a seemingly lost match can be changed with a single correct reflex.

However, if you hit incorrectly when you have no cards, you lose a life instead of a card penalty. If you lose all three lives, you are completely eliminated from the match and can no longer hit the table.

In two-player matches, if one player runs out of cards, their opponent wins the match. This mode offers shorter, more direct, and unforgiving duels.

## HOW TO WIN THE MATCH?

The Queens has multiple victory conditions:

- The player who gets all 52 cards in the deck wins the match instantly. - The player who is the last player alive at the table wins. - In a two-player match, the player who completely eliminates their opponent's cards wins. - If a normal match doesn't conclude within 60 rounds, the player with the most cards is declared the winner.

A round progresses with players who are alive and able to play cards completing their turns around the table. Face card challenges and hitting contests can extend beyond the round's limits; the important thing is to fully resolve the game situation that has begun.

## EXTRA TIME

If two or more players have the same highest card count at the end of round 60, the match does not end in a draw. The card leaders go to extra time.

In extra time, only the tied leader players continue the match. At the end of each full extra time round, the card counts are compared again. Players with the same highest card count advance to the next extra time round, while those behind are eliminated.

This process continues until only one leader remains. Therefore, every decision made until the last card of the match can be important.

## EVERY TABLE IS A DIFFERENT STORY

The Queens comes to life not only through rules, but also through the tension between the players. You can try to anticipate when your opponent will strike, distract them with a fake move, or take a risk when everyone else hesitates. With a large stack of cards on the table, a single right move can change the entire game.

Challenge your friends or online opponents in matches ranging from lively bar atmospheres to themed tables overlooking the sea. Experience a new story in every match with different card sequences, chain face-card challenges, last-minute comebacks, and balances shifting in seconds.

Easy to learn, difficult to master; add The Queens to your wishlist, a game that combines attention, risk management, and reflexes on the same table. Keep your eyes on the table when the cards are dealt—because sometimes it takes only a second to decide the winner.

A Noir Narrative Adventure Set On Mars.

Bab Al-Hadid. The Iron Gate. A mining outpost cut into the basalt of the northern reach, where the air is recycled and the atmospheric processors fight the cold outside. You are Fuad Al-Masry, geologist for the Martian Authority, and you are thirty-seven million kilometers from anywhere you ever wanted to end up.

Features

  • A noir narrative adventure driven by choice and consequence

  • Fully voiced cast and narration

  • A living habitat of characters to meet, question, and understand

  • Collect clues, work the evidence, and uncover a secret ten thousand years patient.

The house always wins — so become the house.

The Rouge Casino is a score-attack roguelite deckbuilder, played across eight complete casino games that share one crooked spine: climb eight antes of Small, Big and Boss blinds, cash out, and spend it all in a shop that sells you ways to cheat. Every table has its own deck to build — you don't just play the wheel, the dice, the reels. You rig them.

THE EIGHT TABLES

  • Roulette Rouge — bet the wheel you built. Remove pockets, load the ball, nudge it after it lands.

  • Blackjack Noir — beat a house that cheats first. Strip the shoe, dye the suits, stack the count.

  • Slot Syndicate — rig your own machine. Rewrite the reel strips symbol by symbol.

  • Craps Crimson — carve the dice, chase the point. Re-pip the faces themselves.

  • Bingo Baroque — one card, daubed to the bone. Cull the cage until your numbers must fall.

  • Darts & Deals — a quiver of crooked arrows. Renumber the board, widen the beds.

  • Domino Dynasty — build the line, hit the fives. Forge duplicate bones, whittle the deadweight.

  • Mahjong Méchant — a wicked wall, a perfect hand. Sweep the junk tiles, smith extra dragons.

THE RUN Beat the target score or lose the run. Boss blinds twist the rules every ante; every eighth ante belongs to a finisher — The House Always Wins, or The Final Audit. Skip a blind for one of 16 tags, level your scoring events with Markers, and spend your winnings on charms, omens, vouchers and booster packs while interest ticks on every $5 you refuse to spend.

THE CHEATING Stamp your own objects — cards, pockets, faces, symbols, balls, wedges, bones, tiles — with enhancements and seals: Gilded, Crimson, Mirrored, Champagne, Bronze reserves, Lucky, Loaded, Wild; Gold, Scarlet, Cobalt, Violet. Shop charms roll Argent, Mirage, Prismatic and Void editions. Every system works in every game.

THE LONG GAME

  • 8 stakes per table, from Ivory to the Rouge Stake — the top tiers add Eternal, Perishable and Rental charms

  • 6 table variants per game and 10 challenges per table (80 in all), each with a persistent ✦ badge

  • Endless mode past Ante 8, where the targets climb without mercy

  • A discovery Collection that fills as you meet the house's charms, omens and bosses — nothing gated, everything earned

  • Seeded runs: copy any run's seed with one click and share the exact same casino with a friend

  • Jacques, the croupier, who explains every table and judges you gently

AT YOUR TABLE, YOUR WAY Full controller and Steam Deck-style navigation, colorblind-safe palette, screen-shake toggle, UI scaling, and separate music/SFX sliders.

HONEST ABOUT THE DISHONESTY The Rouge Casino contains no real-money gambling of any kind — no wagering, no purchasable currency, no microtransactions, no loot boxes. It's a single-purchase game about fictional chips and the fine art of cheating a fictional house.

The Rug Racket is a hands-on restoration sim wrapped around a dark-comedy crime story. You inherit a failing rug-cleaning shop, a bench full of finicky tools, and somebody else's debt.

Every rug through the door is a puzzle of fiber, dye and heat. Every week, the family that holds your paper comes to collect. Get good enough, fast enough, and you buy your way out.

This isn't a one-click clean. Every rug is a five-stage job. Dust, colorfast-test, wash, rinse, extract & dry. Fibers that scorch, dyes that bleed, and stains that set permanently if you reach for the wrong tool or too much heat. Pull the grime back with your own hands and watch a ruined heirloom come back to life.

Inherit a failing business and build it into something. Court a roster of demanding customers, manage a three-axis reputation, weigh four upgrade branches, and survive an overhead curve that never stops climbing. Read the room. The Neurotic Collector won't tolerate a speck; the Art Conservator's antique will scorch if you so much as breathe steam on it.

You don't own this shop free and clear. They do. A weekly tribute, rising pressure across a three-act crime arc, police heat, enforcer visits, and a debt that compounds if you ignore it. Claw your way to the buyout and your independence...
...or fold, in any number of ways.

Special jobs flip the rules. The Flood leaves rugs soaking and breeding mold while your tools run at half power. The Stash is mob work with cash sewn into the pile. Clean it presentable, but dig too deep and you'll find what you were never supposed to see. Master restoration mode for the rugs that look beyond saving.

  • A deep, tactile cleaning craft. 5 stages, real fiber/colorfast/heat rules, a point-of-no-return for the careless.

  • A dark-comedy mob story across three acts, with a buyout win and multiple ways to fold.

  • Push-your-luck special jobs: The Flood (mold) and The Stash (don't overclean).

  • Build a business: customers, reputation, upgrades, events, and legendary moments.

  • Restoration mode for the truly wrecked rugs.

🏢 Work Is a Rule-Based Nightmare

In this company, you begin a seemingly ordinary working life—
go to work, complete tasks, manage your time, and improve your abilities.

But remember:

  • Meet your weekly KPI.

  • Resignation is death.

    Rules come above all.

  • ⏳ Manage Your Time, Shape Yourself

Every day is yours to decide.

You can:

  • Improve your stats to survive increasing pressure

  • Navigate between departments and build relationships

  • Unlock new abilities and actions

  • Balance stress and sanity

    How you spend your days will determine who you become.

⚔ Fight the remnants of enslaved coworkers

In the digital world, the remnants of your coworkers will hunt you.

Each department follows its own combat rules.

Use everything you’ve learned from work to eliminate the KPIs that threaten you.

🧠 Multiple Endings

Every decision you make will affect:

  • The direction of the story

  • Your relationships

  • The stability of the rules

  • Your final outcome

You may end up as just another replaceable worker—or you can flip the table and rewrite the rules.

The Scarlet Thread

In the age of gaslight, Thornecliff Hall on the northern coast is preparing for a coming-of-age celebration. Thirty years ago, a colonel brought a relic home from war: the Scarlet Skein. It is now to pass to a young heiress. Under the terms of the will, its sealed casket must be opened on the night she comes of age.

One case, several narrators

The old butler's Almanac, an inspector's case notes and the private journals of those caught up in the affair tell the story in turn. Each new narrator changes your point of view. Take fresh evidence back to earlier accounts and reconsider what someone said or did. Some things only come to light when you ask one more question, or read an old entry alongside a later one.

Examine objects. Check the records.

Open an envelope and bring the page close to a candle. Hidden writing slowly appears. Compare clothing with lengths of cloth, choose what you need, and decide what to leave in the ledger. Check the tides and phases of the moon. At the pawnbroker's, a grille stands between you and the ledger: you will have to ask about its entries one by one. Ordinary objects and routine records will become evidence as the investigation unfolds.

Re-enact that night

When the accounts don't agree, take part in a re-enactment along the route travelled that night. At a tabletop model, adjust wooden figures, lamplight and the observer's position to test what a witness could actually see. Return to the deduction board and check whether these records support your conclusions. It is not enough to spot a lie. You must also know just how much a truthful statement proves.

A trace of red in black and white

Manor rooms, portraits and paper are rendered in fine 1-bit dots, recalling the copperplate illustrations of old books. The Scarlet Skein stands out in scarlet; red string on the deduction board connects evidence from different journals. Rain at the windows, a quiet fire and the rustle of paper accompany your work. The evidence you keep and the choices you make at the end will decide how the case closes.

Game Description

You got a job as a security guard in a women's only residence!

With nowhere else to go, you, Joo Jihyuk, start working as the only security guard at the Serena Villa, a women's only residence.

However, oddities arise in the apartment from your very first day on the job.

Despite the initial backlash of the residents who didn't want a male security guard,

you still work hard on your job, protecting them by carefully monitoring the CCTV placed in several spots throughout the apartment.

Eventually, the ladies warm up to you, and they start to trust their safety with you... while also trusting you with their heart on top of that?!

So now, you're busy catching the culprit while also catching feelings!

From your vibrant first love acted by Wang Han, to a tough detective baddie.

Plus a cat-like college student, an alluring bar owner, and a glasses-bearing office lady hiding more behind her frames!

These uniquely charming ladies (and more...) are waiting for you all throughout the game.

It could be the ladies, the other thing, or both--

are you ready to get your heartbeat racing?

Character Introduction

Sohan, your cheerful first love

"I will protect you, Jihyuk!"

The world is a better place whenever she's around, carrying the warmth of sunlight with her presence.

Sohan, your childhood friend, was your protector back then.

You never thought you'd get to see her again after losing contact once, but here we are now!

Beautiful new memories start blooming between the two reunited souls.

Yeonwoo, a lingerie company OL full of secrets

"Well, in that case... Do you want to see more here?"

This resident has a timid, quiet personality that awakens your protective instincts each time.

...or so you thought.

Behind her glasses, her strong gaze pierces through you to an unsettling extent.

What other secrets is she hiding?

Woohyun, a tough police detective

"Hold my waist tight. I won't take responsibility if you fall."

The cool, easygoing detective who always refuses your help, saying she doesn't need it.

Her gaze never falters, not even in the presence of dangerous criminals,

but you catch the slight twinkle in her eyes when she's with you!

Wait, Detective, are you blushing?

Hyeji, a cat-like college student

"U-ugh! Why would you worry about me?!"

Hyeji is like a grumpy kitten who hisses at you all day.

As she opens her heart to you, though, you see how she's a tsundere who cares more than she lets show.

She has also seen the stalker up close, so what's her secret?!

Gyeoul, an alluring bar owner

"What's weighing on your shoulders, Jihyuk? Wanna talk about it over a drink?"

A short conversation with her melts the day's wariness after a long day of work.

Each and every one of bar owner Gyeoul's moves is graceful yet meticulously composed.

Be careful not to let your guard down too much around her...

...because you'll get intoxicated by her ravishing charms.

Key Features

Interactive story from a first-person POV

The story unfolds from Jihyuk's point of view!

Explore the building in first-person POV,

checking the CCTV and patrolling around spots.

Your choice will build your relationship with the ladies.

A diverse mix of heroines, featuring Korean and Chinese actresses

Meet a wider and more distinctive cast of heroines brought to life

through the first collaboration between Korean and Chinese actors!

From a first love who shines like sunlight, to a charismatic detective,

a cat-like college student, and a heroine with unexpected hidden charms,

each character brings her own personality and story to the screen.

Even better acting and cinematic visuals

Our second collaboration with the production team behind Heroines Through My Lens!

Experience richer visuals, more natural performances,

and a deeper sense of immersion in this upgraded interactive drama.

Multiple endings shaped by your choices

Hidden choices and branching routes are waiting to be discovered.

Even the smallest decision can change your relationships with the heroines,

the direction of the story, and the ending you reach.

Play through the game multiple times and discover the different outcomes for yourself.

Special appearances hidden throughout the game

Eunbi from the first season of Five Hearts Under One Roof,

Team Leader Sung from Heroines Through My Lens,

and Qiao Zhien, a hot and rising Chinese FMV star!

Find familiar faces in the nooks and crannies of Serena Villa,

and enjoy a new experience with the actors you know and love!

About Us

Hello!

We are Storytaco, an interactive game development studio.

We are very excited to introduce this new project as our second collaboration with video production company WHYNOT Media.

This title is an interactive FMV created together by a Korean production team featuring Korean and Chinese actors. With the addition of Chinese actress Wang Han, the game brings an even wider range of charm and personality to the screen.

Our goal was to create a story that players can connect with and enjoy across languages and borders, and we hope this project becomes the beginning of many new encounters.

We will continue working hard to bring you even better interactive content.

Thank you for your love and support always!

Shonanoka — the Buddhist memorial service held on the seventh day after a death.

Tsubaki Soemon, who built a fortune from seven companies, has died. Cause: heart failure.

You arrive as a law clerk entrusted with his will, to stay until the seventh-day memorial.

On the desk in his study, a single sake cup, washed and left face-down. That is all.

Only ten moves before the memorial

There are 13 places and people you can visit — the annex, the kitchen, the storehouse,

the herb garden, the temple, the clinic, the teahouse on the pass, and the suspects themselves.

But you only get 10 free actions before the service on the seventh day.

You cannot see everything. What waited down the path you didn't take stays unknown.

Evidence stacks in three columns: motive, opportunity, proof

You may rise at the incense offering and name anyone — as long as your journal holds

at least one line about them. Against a blank page, you cannot get to your feet.

The question is not whether you can accuse, but what your accusation is worth.

Name them with all three columns and you reach the truth. Name them without, and even

the right person yields only an accusation without certainty.

Each night, your journal writes itself — in your words

Evidence gathered during the day is composed into your journal at night.

Gather by day, arrange by night. No two playthroughs produce the same journal.

Four suspects. Any of them could be the killer

The eldest son, the second wife, the illegitimate son, the old steward.

Each is hiding something, whether or not they are the killer.

One of the four is chosen as the killer, so the same house yields different evidence.

The eldest son — Tsubaki Soichi (50)

Managing director of the group. Raised as the only heir.

He lies. In an executive's polite phrasing, with his irritation wrapped inside.

"Good of you to come. So, what is it you've come to check on today?"

The second wife — Tsubaki Sayo (51)

A former nurse. Eight years his second wife; she saw him through to the end.

She keeps silent. She tells no lies. She simply doesn't answer.

"No. It is nothing."

The illegitimate son — Sano Ryo (24)

An outsider who appeared at the funeral. His mother has passed; the surname is his alone.

There is no way to check. His story holds. There is nothing to test it against.

"I was at my hotel. ...All night."

The steward — Tsukamoto Juzo (66)

A retainer with no blood tie to the family. Forty-five years in service, since the previous generation.

Too honest. He answers before you ask, with the times and the figures attached.

"Certainly. Hour by hour, then."

The eldest son, the second wife, the illegitimate son, the old steward.

Each is hiding something, whether or not they are the killer.

One of the four is chosen as the killer, so the same house yields different evidence.

Four endings

The Truth (three columns, right person) / An Accusation Without Certainty

(right person, thin evidence) / A False Charge (wrong person) /

Unsolved (you named no one). Saying nothing is an ending too, and it is recorded as one.

Replay to open all four cases

Roughly 40–90 minutes per playthrough. Bring a culprit's name to light and that case is bound into your Case File,

and the next run picks a culprit you haven't seen. A case you couldn't crack returns on the next run. Even after all four names are known, you can revisit an opened case to find the evidence you missed.

Your investigative habits are reflected back at you at the end of each run.

The people at the heart of the case

The deceased — Tsubaki Soemon (72)

The man who built seven companies. A heart condition. Every night at nine, a single go of sake, alone in the annex.

He had a notarial will drawn up fourteen days before he died. At his last supper, he told the family:

"I have made a new will. It is in Mr. Okuma's keeping. It will be opened after the shonanoka. Each of you had best think carefully."

You

A clerk at the Okuma Law Office. Your name and gender are never revealed.

Entrusted with the will, you stay in the house until the seventh-day rite.

Every night, you write down what you saw that day in your journal.

The family lawyer — Okuma

Your employer, and the Tsubaki family's lawyer. He was present when the notarial will was made.

From outside the house, he advises you by phone and by letter.

"...Don't wear yourself down. Your work is not to judge. It is to watch. Until the seal is broken on the seventh day."

The sister — Takato Sakie

The deceased's younger sister. Not invited to the funeral, she speaks of the Tsubaki family from outside, over the phone.

"Still in that house. ...You'd do well not to stay too long. That house puts a stoop in anyone who stays in it."

Other characters

The maid — Yoshie

Talkative, and knows the daily life of the Tsubaki house inside out.

"Well, well, come in. I've just this minute finished stewing the aubergines—"

The priest — Koun

Keeper of the family temple, and Soemon's regular opponent at the board game go.

"Come to pay your respects, have you. ...No. Not respects. Not with that face."

The old doctor — Narazaki

The town clinic. Fifty years of watching this town's births and deaths.

"...Fifty years of it now. I brought the children of this town into the world, and then I sat with their parents at the end. Lately it's the sitting at the end, and nothing else."

The teahouse keeper — Umekichi

The teahouse at the pass, partway up the road from the town into the mountains.

"...Police, are you. No. No, you're not. Police hardly ever order the cakes."

About the Demo

The demo is a separate case, written for the demo alone, and you can play it from beginning to ending.

The culprit in the demo is always the same person. In exchange, not one of the four truths in the full game is revealed.

Solve it or fail it — the case in this house is still entirely ahead of you.

What's included

  • 40–90 minutes per playthrough; roughly 3–4 hours to see all four truths

  • Japanese, English and Simplified Chinese text (no voice acting)

  • Keyboard and mouse (partial controller support)

  • Save anywhere; progress carries across playthroughs

About Streaming and Videos

You are free to stream, upload videos, make clips, and post review videos. No permission is needed in advance, and no notification afterward. Monetization is not restricted.

If your video contains major spoilers, we ask that you indicate this clearly in the title or description.

For full details, please see the streaming guidelines for this title on the official Maru Works website.

The Sixth Dice is a dice-building roguelike that fuses poker hand combos. Roll five-tier dice, re-roll, modify faces, and shift tiers to form pairs, full houses, straights, or five-of-a-kind to crush monsters. Randomly acquire runes, skills, and relics to forge your own build, and battle through 8 chapters and 24 fights. Defeat the final boss to unlock the Sixth Dice and enter endless climbing. Every roll is a clash of strategy and luck.

Thirty-two children. One night. Not one of them cried out.

In the winter of 1996, thirty-two children were found dead in their beds at St. Adela's Orphanage on Blackmoor Hill. No fire. No wounds. No sign of forced entry. Three separate investigations closed with the same sentence: cause undetermined.

The only adult in the building that night was a carer named Mary Doyle. Mary vanished afterwards — and she took the institution's youngest resident with her, four-year-old Stephen.

Thirty years later, Mary died. She left behind a box, a letter, and one request: take the box back to the orphanage.

Seven sins, six seals, one lie

In 1911, Father Thomas Ward preached on this hill, opened a book, and something answered. There were seven of them — one for each of the seven deadly sins. Ward managed to bind six, each to an object: a lamp, a ring, a chalice, a mirror, a book cover, a box. The moment he called the seventh, his hand shook and the ritual was left unfinished.

The seals were never broken. They were only bound. And a binding has to be renewed every generation.

Ward's last note ends with a warning: one of the six is not like the others. It talks. It persuades. It helps.

Throughout the game a voice on the radio will guide you. You decide which question to ask: "what should I do", or "who told me to do it"?

Gameplay

An inventory that takes up space

Your bag is a grid. Every item has a shape, you can rotate it, and you cannot carry everything. The flashlight, the bat, or the candle you need for the ritual? Your call — and every time, something gets left behind. Build your base with storage chests and a crafting bench.

Light is a weapon, darkness is an enemy

You can swing a bat at the Soulless, or throw a chair at them. But you cannot touch the ghost children — only your flashlight's ultraviolet mode destroys them. And the battery runs out.

Puzzles without panels

No puzzle traps you in a menu. You turn the three-dial symbol lock while standing in the room — if something comes up behind you, you have to turn and run. To find the symbols you must inspect the paintings under ultraviolet light. Some of those paintings watch you back. When the lock opens the painting changes — but only while you are not looking.

Rituals

Closing a seal means performing a ritual. Free the caged candles, light them in the right order, draw the sigil patterns with your own hand. An unfinished ritual does not kill them. It only angers them.

Mirrors are doors

Stand before a mirror with the right object and you cross to the other side. You will come back, yes. But not as the same person.

Inspired by the Nart epic, the game tells the story of Sosruko, a warrior born from stone.

He is a central figure in Caucasian mythology, known for his heroic deeds, cunning, and immense strength.

Experience focused, linear progression with cinematic boss battles and skill-based combat.

Choose your fighting style:

• Sword — balanced melee with reliable blocking

• Dual Daggers — a high-risk, high-reward style focused on precise deflects

• Bow — a hybrid ranged and close-combat style, allowing both distance pressure and direct engagement

Each style offers a different way to experience the same battles and enemies.

Use stone-based abilities to enhance your combat, and unleash Rampage state to crush everything in your path.

A third-person action game focused on combat, where every encounter requires adaptation, decision-making, and precise execution.

“We offer hymns to the gods. The gods answer with a lament.”

War between humans and fiends flares anew, but the border village of Qinghe has already been forgotten.

At five years old, YunXi loses her mother overnight. When she wakes, a bracelet called Heartcandle rests upon her wrist, and a voice from another world stirs within her mind. That voice is your soul.

A mysterious summoning binds your fate to hers. You accompany YunXi through childhood and adolescence, watching her grow up alongside YangYuan and YangYu'er—and witnessing the calamity deep in the mountains that tears their lives apart.

When YunXi turns eighteen, the northern front faces a crisis. The garrison withdraws from Shadow Bone Tower, leaving the village exposed. YunXi and YangYuan set out in search of the missing YangYu'er, and of answers to the silence her mother left behind.

Ahead lie restless spirits beneath the Blind Moon, people abandoned by war, and the inner demons no one wishes to face.

You can speak within YunXi’s mind, but you cannot live her life for her. Every choice leaves a mark. And what begins as a search for her mother may become something else: learning to live for those who are still by her side.

Features

  • A journey together, beginning in childhood
    From a wooden cottage and herb garden to mountain streams and roads scarred by war, watch YunXi grow from a child left behind into someone who can choose her own path.

  • Two souls, one shared journey
    You are the “second voice” within YunXi’s consciousness. At crucial moments, your judgment shapes her state of mind and her actions.

  • Choices that carry a cost
    Attachment, self-preservation, reason, and the desire to protect others all leave their imprint on YunXi’s inner world, affecting relationships, combat conditions, and the price of moving forward. Failure does not simply erase everything. Its scars remain part of the story.

  • Two forms of combat
    Deploy companions and arrange formations to face bandits, beasts, and armies in conventional battles. In soul combat, fire Soul Stones and summon cards across a spiritual game board, breaking through manifestations of your enemies’ desires to reach the deepest recesses of their souls.

  • The Hundred Souls evolution system
    One hundred Soul Stones take on the seven sins, undergo purification, or become locked in their state through battles and story events. Over time, they record how you fight and the choices you make, forming a portrait of your soul that is yours alone.

  • Bonds that change with the journey
    YangYuan, YangYu'er, and the people you meet each carry their own wounds and ways of living. Your choices affect their trust, their condition, and how you move forward together.

  • Dark fantasy beneath three waning moons
    The Iron Moon, Blood Moon, and Blind Moon hold sway over order, werewolves, and restless spirits. Ink-wash landscapes, a spirit-sight alive with strange colors, and original music bring a beautiful yet perilous continent to life.

Content advisory: Contains depictions of war, loss of loved ones, physical injury, hostile spirits, and psychological distress.

You are the heroine of a fantasy story… except you're a sword!

Světlavoda, an old town sitting on the edge of an empire. Railways and shipping lines pass through it, so its languages mix and its faiths overlap, and generations of ambition and trauma lie buried beneath its streets. And you are just the Sword in Stone, asleep for years deep inside Světlavoda library.

To you, none of it ever seemed to matter… until the day you woke up. You're given one chance: take human form, step into this city, and come to know, care,and love.

■ Starting from a manuscript in the library basement, uncover layer by layer the secrets about yourself — and about this city.

■ A text-based city life sim: explore Světlavoda freely, work to earn your keep, and meet residents of very different personalities and backgrounds as the days and nights go by.

■ An alternate-history fantasy setting rooted in Central European history — fractured nations, vanished peoples, migrating cultures, and the fault lines of language and identity… retold through the small details of everyday life.

■ Rich branching story and multiple endings — there's no single correct path, only the one you're willing to answer for.

■ Friendship, challenges, adventure, love, marriage, history, trauma, struggle, order… but does any of it actually matter to you?

====================================================

Disclaimer:

When the Sword in Stone began planning in June 2024, it was conceived as a fairly traditional dating-sim with a female protagonist, so most of the interactable characters are male. Over the course of development, I gradually came to see other possibilities for TSIS, and so the game was gradually broadened. In short, if this makes you uncomfortable, please stop playing.

I could try to argue that, given the era this story is set in, you'd rarely run into other women on the street — but that would only highlight how poorly I've written my characters, wouldn't it?

====================================================

Basic Controls:

Click options with the mouse, or use the number-key shortcuts.

The spacebar skips the typewriter effect. Or simply clicking the textbox.

====================================================

【From dev】

When the ideas taking shape in my mind left me too restless to sit still, I knew there was no turning back. I've poured out my experiences, my thoughts, and the visions that have haunted me day after day, sharing them through the convenience of the internet with anyone genuinely interested. I've watched my story gradually take form, my heart filled with joy, and so I sincerely hope it can bring a little happiness to every passerby who happens to arrive here.

Any published work must endure the scrutiny of its audience, and I've poured my whole heart and body into this one — what's left of me has no strength to withstand accusations that go beyond the work itself.

"Persons attempting to find a motive in this narrative will be prosecuted; persons attempting to find a moral in it will be banished; persons attempting to find a plot in it will be shot."

— Mark Twain

Forge With Hammer and Fire

The Swordsmith is a 2D crafting roguelite built around one idea: you truly make every sword yourself. A reclusive swordsmith, an old promise, and 70 days to forge a blade worthy of sealing the Rift.

🔨 Real Forging, Not a Menu

Work the bellows, swing the hammer, quench, grind, and inscribe — five hands-on QTE stages with live furnace temperature, pressure and purity. Every strike is written into the steel. Same recipe, a hundred different blades.

⚔️ The Swords Are the Heroes

Your forged blades fight on their own: vanguard crushers, mid-row fencers, back-row spirit casters. Seven elements (Fire/Ice/Thunder/Wind/Water/Poison/Earth) resonate and counter each other — elemental resonance, style certification, combo greed. The build depth grows with every forge.

🗺️ A New Jianghu Every Run

Roguelite expeditions: hunts, encounters, sword rituals, caravans... every map is unique to its seed. Six sword archetypes plus legendary blueprints (Yuchang, Zhanlu, Tai'a...), living materials with individual rolls — the science of feedstock never ends.

💫 Blades Have Souls

Five battles together and your sword speaks. Your hand-drawn blade is its true form — at the Drawing Desk, your finger is the brush, and no two players' swords look alike.

🌙 Someone Is Waiting for You

A wisp of soul-light lives by your forge, growing brighter with your bond — Glimmer, Firefly, Moonlight, Sunblaze, Everlight. Multiple endings, New Game+ legacy — every road has its own ending.

Beyond the Ending

Clear the Spirit Rift to unlock the Endless Tower — infinite floors, custom seed challenges, and your strongest formation carved in stone.

a life, itemized.

You wake up in Corvid City with a coffee to try, a job to find, and rent that does not care about your feelings. So you live. You work shifts, meet the regulars, take photos for the Tourism Board, ride a skateboard you probably cannot afford, and make a thousand small choices that feel like nothing at the time.

They were not nothing. Something was counting.

When your time is up, and it will be up, you receive THE RECEIPT: every kindness, every shortcut, every held door and quiet lie, added up and handed back to you. Then you are sorted. Where you end up is between you and the arithmetic.

In the box:

  • A hand-built PS2-era city that actually lives: jobs, shops, weather, regulars who remember you

  • A full life, start to finish, in around 90 minutes

  • Eight jobs, a phone full of apps, a camera, and a skateboard

  • An ending. A real one. Most games don't have one.

  • Whatever is on the other side of THE RECEIPT (you will see)

No tutorials nag you. No meter tells you if you are being good. You just live, and it is all written down.

Made and developed by aninsecurecarrot.

BECOME A TRAM DRIVER

Take control of a classic tram and guide it along scenic routes inspired by Central and Eastern Europe of the 2000s.

Operate the tram’s systems, navigate challenging sections of track and harsh weather conditions, keep to the schedule, and ensure passenger comfort while traveling between residential districts, suburbs, and industrial areas.

KEY FEATURES

Realistic tram handling
Learn how the systems and electronics of a classic tram work. The car’s weight, inertia, and track condition demand careful, attentive driving.

Atmospheric city
Explore a fictional city inspired by Central and Eastern Europe in the mid-2000s: panel housing districts, forest stretches, industrial areas, and a historic center.

Dynamic driving conditions
Weather, temperature, and rail condition directly affect the tram’s behavior and require you to adapt your driving style.

Challenging route sections
Worn curved rails, gradients, and speed restrictions will test your control and precision.

Driver responsibility
Follow the timetable, carry passengers, and keep an eye on their comfort level.

REALISM

Driving a tram isn’t as easy as it may seem.

A 16-ton machine is sensitive to speed, weather, and track condition, so the driver must stay focused and precise. Slippery rails, frost, worn curves, and other infrastructure quirks will test your skills and your ability to adapt to real-world conditions.

Passengers trust your professionalism and want to arrive on time. Can you live up to that trust?

THE WORLD AROUND YOU

A fictional yet richly detailed city awaits, inspired by Eastern and Central Europe in the mid-2000s.

Panel housing districts, forest sections, industrial zones, and an old town center create a varied and atmospheric urban environment.

Explore the city in any season, at any time of day, and in different weather—conditions directly affect the tram’s handling and present new challenges.

WHAT’S AVAILABLE IN EARLY ACCESS

In Early Access you can:

• drive two routes with a total length of about 15 km
• master a classic tram with detailed, functional systems
• test yourself on demanding sections with worn curved rails
• operate the tram in different weather and across seasons

Follow the timetable, feel the inertia of a heavy car, and carefully control your speed to avoid violations.

GAME DEVELOPMENT

The Tram is an atmospheric tram driving simulator created by people passionate about urban transport. Its journey is just beginning, and we would be happy to grow the game together with the community.

In Early Access, the game already includes the core driving mechanics, two routes, and basic simulation systems. In the future, we plan to expand the city map, introduce new trams, add gameplay mechanics, and develop additional routes.

We will be closely following your feedback and suggestions!

TINY CARS. HUGE TROUBLE.

Choose your vehicle, equip a cannon, and turn giant furniture, toys, and gardens into arcade combat arenas. Drive, jump, fly with nitro, and open fire while trying to stay on your wheels.

FOUR WAYS TO WIN

• Turbo Rupture: leap between disappearing platforms and become the last car standing.

• Chase: catch the marked player, steal the target position, and escape everyone else.

• 5v5 Battle: work with your team and be the first to reach the elimination limit.

• Free-for-All: every rival is a target and every elimination counts.

MASTER THE GROUND AND THE AIR

Use ramps, furniture, and obstacles to gain altitude. Control your car in midair, save enough nitro to correct your landing, and fire your cannon to destabilize or knock rivals out of the arena.

PLAY YOUR WAY

• Online battles for up to 10 players.

• Quick Match and private rooms.

• Local matches against bots with three difficulty levels.

• Five toy-scale arenas.

• Turbo School teaches you how to drive, fly, and fight.

BUILD YOUR CAR

Combine bodies, wheels, engine sounds, cannons, projectiles, nitro trails, explosions, and elimination markers. Build a machine that stands out even in the middle of the chaos.

FREE TO PLAY. NEVER PAY TO WIN.
