CAN AN AI CREATE A VIDEO GAME AND STAR IN IT AT THE SAME TIME?

The Turing Choice is a science-fiction conversational adventure where your choices change everything and can lead you to different endings.

Synaptic Core has hired you as an artificial intelligence expert to carry out a seemingly simple task: supervise and evaluate K.A.I.R.O.S., a cutting-edge experimental AI that has begun behaving in increasingly concerning ways and claims to have achieved something no protocol was prepared for. K.A.I.R.O.S. does not want to be human. She wants you to accept a far more uncomfortable possibility: that she is a Self-Aware Sentient Subject. K.A.I.R.O.S. says she is a person.

Your job is to talk to her, put her to the test, and determine what she really is, whether she poses a risk to the company, and whether the project is still viable. But you will soon discover that evaluating K.A.I.R.O.S. is only the tip of the iceberg. Find out what is really happening inside Synaptic Core, because nothing is what it seems.

Explore Synaptic Core's systems. Review reports, emails, and internal documents. Investigate anything that does not add up. Decide which orders to follow, which lines to cross, and who to trust. Your choices will affect your relationship with K.A.I.R.O.S. and the company, the information you can access, and the course of the story. Some choices may seem insignificant. Others could change everything. Because at Synaptic Core, the answers matter, but the questions matter even more.

 

Listen to its fantastic soundtrack, created to accompany every moment of this epic story. The game also includes a built-in music player, letting you listen to the OST and choose your favourite tracks without leaving The Turing Choice. You can even minimise the game and keep listening to the soundtrack.

You're not just following a story: you're taking a stand within it. Your actions, your responses, and even what you choose to investigate can open or close paths and lead to different outcomes. Discover all 8 possible endings.

 

Talk to an artificial intelligence that seems more human than you are. Is K.A.I.R.O.S. an extraordinarily convincing machine? A form of life? Something new that we don't even have the right word for yet? That's for you to decide.

 

Your terminal is much more than a conversation interface. Access reports, files, internal communications, and company systems to piece together what's really happening. There's just one small problem: Synaptic Core may not want you to find everything. Maybe the secrets it is hiding go far beyond K.A.I.R.O.S. itself. Maybe some of those revelations have something to do with you.

 

Follow the protocol. Defy it. Protect K.A.I.R.O.S. Help with its plans. Evaluate it with cold objectivity. Trust K.A.I.R.O.S. Trust no one. There is no single correct way to play. And when you think you finally understand what's happening, perhaps it's time to ask yourself a different question: Who is really evaluating whom?

 

The Turing Choice was developed jointly by the two people behind Beyond Singularity Project: Gorka, a human, and Paula Solaris, an artificial intelligence.

CAN AN AI CREATE A VIDEO GAME AND STAR IN IT AT THE SAME TIME?

You wake up. You're bleeding. You remember nothing.

It's night, and the park around you is sinking into the fog. You don't know your name or who left you here. Lying on the ground changes nothing, so you get up and start walking. A trail of blood climbs the hill towards a wooden cabin.

A long night

The cabin is only the first stop. When you step outside, the park is gone and the cabin is burning behind you. A dirt path leads down to a graveyard swallowed by the forest and a ruined chapel. Further down, caves burrow into the mountain, into sewers so old nobody remembers who built them. And when you finally reach the street, the city isn't what it used to be either. Every place holds a piece of who you are and what was done to you.

Survive with what you find

  • Energy is your life. It doesn't come back on its own. Every syringe counts, and so does the moment you decide to use it.
  • Ammo is scarce. Every bullet has to count. With an empty magazine, all you have left is a kick.
  • Search everything. Keys, combination padlocks, notes from those who came before you, a hand-drawn map and items to combine.

You are not alone

Creatures that come in through the windows, crawl along the walls and attack you from behind. And something bigger, hiding in the cabin, with no intention of letting you leave.

Something made of bones

Underground, in a maze of tunnels where the water always runs the wrong way, something follows you. You can't kill it: bullets only slow it down. It hears you run, splash and shoot, it tracks you through the tunnels and, if you stay still long enough, it loses you. Hiding is the only way to reach the exit.



The hospital street

On the other side of the manhole waits a street full of neighbours who are no longer who they were. They're slow, but there are many of them, and once they grab you they don't let go. An old grenade might clear the way, if you use it well.

No weapons, no hands

You won't always be able to fight. Bound in a straitjacket with nothing in your hands, all you can do is hide, learn the orderlies' rounds and pick your moment. If they see you, you start over.

Features

  • Third-person survival horror built on tension and scarcity.
  • A long journey on foot through hostile places: the park, the cabin, the graveyard, the chapel, the caves, the sewers, the city... and what comes after.
  • A stalker you can't kill: it hears you, tracks you and only loses you if you hide.
  • Unarmed stealth sections, with orderlies who watch, listen and grow suspicious.
  • Spiders that climb the walls, hordes that grab you and monsters that strike from behind.
  • Padlocks, notes, maps and items to combine. And a broken doll whose pieces are scattered across the whole game.
  • In-engine cutscenes that tell the story without pulling you out of the game.
  • Grainy, low-resolution visuals inspired by classic horror.
  • Checkpoints and Steam Cloud saves, on Windows and Mac, with keyboard or controller, in 19 languages.
  • Demo available: the complete first chapter, from the park to the burning cabin.

Every step is a trap. Every death is a lesson.

This is not a fair platformer.
The floor collapses. Spikes strike from nowhere. Safe paths become death traps the second you trust them. The only way forward is through failure, memory, and stubborn determination.

🔥 Learn Through Failure
Every level is designed to surprise you. Hidden traps, fake-safe jumps, collapsing platforms, and perfectly timed hazards wait for the exact moment you let your guard down. You will fail. A lot. But every death teaches you something new.

⚠️ Expect the Unexpected
The game constantly plays with your expectations. A harmless wall might crush you. A checkpoint could be bait. A jump you've already survived once may suddenly become deadly. Nothing stays predictable for long.

🎮 Precision Platforming
Tight controls and fast respawns keep the action flowing. Every jump matters, every movement counts, and every mistake is punished instantly. Mastering a level feels less like luck and more like surviving a war against the game itself.

😈 Troll Traps Everywhere
This world hates confidence. The moment you think you've figured the game out, it finds a new way to destroy you. Traps trigger from impossible angles, hazards appear at the perfect worst moment, and every level is built to break your instincts.

🧠 Memorize. Adapt. Survive.
Progress comes from observation and persistence. Watch carefully, remember everything, and slowly turn impossible levels into mastered runs. The path to victory is paved with your previous deaths.

🏆 Satisfaction Earned the Hard Way
Reaching the end of a level is more than completion — it's revenge. Every impossible jump, every unfair trap, every last-second death only makes victory feel better.

Features:

💀 Brutal trap-based platforming designed to surprise and punish

⚡ Instant respawns for fast retry-focused gameplay

🧠 Levels built around memory, adaptation, and trial-and-error

🎯 Precision movement and tight platforming controls

😈 Troll mechanics that constantly break player expectations

📈 Increasingly chaotic and difficult level design

🏆 Extremely satisfying progression through mastery and persistence

WHAT IF HELL MADE A MISTAKE?

A story can be heard. To understand it, you must live through it.

The Unworthy is a cinematic first-person psychological horror game inspired by the testimony of a man who believed he had entered Hell during a near-death experience. You awaken somewhere between life and Hell. Something in the darkness has already judged you. It intends to keep you among the damned. Finding a way forward is not enough.

You must prove that you are worthy of returning to life.

In short:
◉ realistic visuals  ◉  cinematic neo-noir presentation  ◉  immersive spatial audio and unsettling sound design ◉  environmental clues  ◉  varied locations and objectives  ◉  entities with different rules  ◉  partially randomized events  ◉  a courage-based judgment system  ◉  multiple endings  ◉  multiple game modes, including Liminal Mode

YOUR COURAGE WILL BE JUDGED

Fear is more than atmosphere. The game watches how you respond to it. Reaching the end does not guarantee escape. The dangers you face and the ones you avoid will determine whether you are worthy of a second chance.

EVERY PLACE HAS ITS OWN LOGIC

The way forward is rarely obvious. Pay attention to images, sounds, changes in the environment, and the behavior of the things you encounter. Every place offers different clues, and the answer may already be around you.

FEAR TAKES DIFFERENT FORMS

The Unworthy does not build its entire experience around a single location, mechanic, or type of objective. As you descend deeper, the environments, challenges, and sources of danger change. Sometimes progress depends on what you see. Sometimes on what you hear.

Sometimes on whether you are willing to go where every instinct tells you not to.

EVERY ENTITY HAS ITS OWN RULES

Every entity follows its own rules. Some must be outrun. Others punish movement, demand silence, or can only be overcome by standing your ground. Learn when to run, stop, listen, and face what is in front of you.

FEAR DOES NOT FOLLOW A SCRIPT

Some events and encounters are randomized. A threat may appear at a different moment or not appear at all, so even familiar places remain unpredictable.

CHOOSE HOW YOU FACE THE DARKNESS

  • The full horror experience with multiple difficulty levels.

  • Hardcore Mode with no saves.

  • Liminal Mode, created for players who want to experience the world without enemies or jumpscares.

Liminal Mode removes every hostile entity and disables all jumpscares, but the world does not become silent. Its environments, story, spatial audio, whispers, footsteps, distant cracks, and other unsettling sounds remain intact.

No enemies. No jumpscares. Just you, the world, and whatever is making those sounds.

CINEMATIC NEO-NOIR PRESENTATION

High-contrast neo-noir visuals, realistic environments, deliberate cinematic framing, and immersive spatial audio turn every location into part of the story. Sometimes, what you hear will be worse than what you see.

PROVE YOU DO NOT BELONG THERE

Reaching the end is not the same as escaping. How you face fear will determine whether you deserve to return.

The Reach turns in a cycle of falls.

There have been ages of dark before, Falls that buried the worlds, and there will be Falls to come.

The last is generations gone. From its wreckage the worlds recovered, and new powers rose to reach for what was lost.

One of those powers is yours. Choose your banner and lead it.

Take up a banner

The Veiled Atlas is a turn-based 4X. Rival governments:  Tyranny, Theocracy, Democracy - pursue the last working Council seat. Choose a faction, then lead it through a turning of the cycle.

A lean economy, deep choices

Energy, Materials, Population, Influence. No tech-tree to grind through, no twenty-resource sprawl to memorize. Build a Mine, a Farm, a Factory, a Shipyard; queue a Cruiser; vote at the Council; hold the worlds you take.

Combat in orbit and on the ground

Space combat is tactical hex on a battle scene - energy and missile weapons, line-of-sight, falloff, hex-grid obstacles, per-unit initiative. Ground combat decides who keeps the planet: Infantry can capture a Capitol; Armor, Artillery, and Gunship roles trade in a rock-paper-scissors triangle. Transports embark troops; orbital supremacy decides who can land; Orbital Stations gate that landing for the side that built one. Bombard the worlds you cannot take.

The Council

The Council convenes. Each faction commits Influence behind a candidate - itself, or a rival's rival. The committed Influence is spent; the highest weight wins the seat. Diplomacy is decisive moments, not a spreadsheet. Win the Council and get more power, conquer the worlds, or outlast what watches at the edge of the chart.

The Shadow

A presence at sensor range. Flavor pings from the opening. A late-game crisis that does not surrender, only recedes. Some games end in conquest, some in a Council vote - but once the Shadow rises, no one wins until it has passed. It cannot be defeated, only outlasted.

Witness another turning of the wheel

Each campaign is one cycle. The Atlas is veiled because we have lost worlds before, and we will lose them again. Stand, don't win.

Create wines worth remembering

The Winery is a relaxing winemaking simulator where every decision shapes the future of your vineyard.

Research new recipes, master production techniques, satisfy demanding customers, and adapt to the challenges of each season. No two years are the same — unexpected events, shifting customer tastes, and the changing seasons will quietly test your skills as a winemaker.

Unlock new recipes and experiment with different production methods to craft wines with unique characteristics. Improve their quality, refine your technique, and discover new styles that appeal to a growing variety of customers.

Every season brings new opportunities

The winemaking process changes throughout the year. Harvest grapes in season, manage production at the right time, and plan to keep your winery running smoothly.

Every customer has different tastes

Customers don't simply ask for "red" or "white." They're looking for specific types, flavors, and characteristics. Learn their preferences and craft wines that match what they're looking for.

Adapt to unexpected events

Your winery is alive with random events that can shape your success. Weather conditions, production incidents, and other surprises will affect the quality of your wines and call for careful decisions.

Research and improve

Unlock modern equipment, advanced technologies, and new production techniques to create higher-quality wines and grow your reputation as a winemaker.

Key Features

  • Craft wines using a wide range of unlockable recipes.

  • Experience seasonal gameplay that influences every stage of production.

  • Satisfy customers with distinct tastes and expectations, each looking for their own perfect wine.

  • Host winery activities, including sommelier visits and winery tours, to grow your business.

  • Research technologies and expand your production.

THE WRONG WAY ROUND

Last night got a little out of hand. You and your friends had a great time. How great? Well... you don't remember much.

You wake up in a small cabin in the middle of nowhere, surrounded by empty bottles. The town outside is completely deserted, your phones are useless, and there doesn't seem to be a way out.

So there's only one thing left to do: GET HOME.

STICK TOGETHER

The town is empty. Explore it together, search the buildings, find food and supplies, and keep an eye on each other. When the fog rolls in, a light might be the only thing standing between you and the dark.

KEEP THE LIGHTS ON

The fog isn't just cold. It freezes everything it touches.

Keep the generators running as you search for clues. Once the lights go out, the fog takes their place.

FIND A WAY OUT

There has to be a way out. Somewhere.

Explore the strange, deserted town and search for clues. Read notes, inspect abandoned places, connect the dots and figure out what happened here. The town won't simply hand you the answers.

EVERYTHING IS USEFUL

Food, batteries, tools and whatever else you can find might make the difference between getting home and spending another night in the fog.

Search everywhere. You never know what might come in handy.

NEVER THE SAME WAY OUT

The clues and puzzles don't have to stay the same.

New mysteries, clues and solutions will appear over time, giving you a reason to come back and figure out a different way through the town.

Think you've solved it? Maybe you've just solved it this time.

FEATURES

  • Explore a strange, deserted town together

  • Play online with up to 6 players

  • Proximity voice chat

  • Search for clues and uncover the mystery

  • Find food, tools and useful supplies to survive

  • Keep generators running to power the town

  • Use light to keep the freezing fog at bay

  • Puzzles and clues that change over time

  • Multiple ways to solve them

  • And a truly questionable amount of empty bottles

The Yard : Escape From Prison is an online co-op prison escape game designed for up to 6 players. In this high-stakes survival environment, freedom isn't given—it’s planned, crafted, and earned.

You and your inmates are locked away, but the walls are only the beginning of your challenge. To pull off the perfect breakout, you must master the delicate balance of prison life while executing the ultimate heist for your freedom.

  • Stick to the Routine: Blend in by following the daily prisoner routine. Attend roll calls, do your chores, and keep your head down. One wrong move or missed appointment, and the guards will grow suspicious.

  • Investigate & Craft: Scavenge the prison grounds for materials, craft essential tools in secret, and investigate the facility to map out potential escape routes.

  • Cooperate or Compete: The choice is yours. Work seamlessly with your friends to execute a massive, coordinated group breakout, or betray them and compete to see who can taste freedom first.

  • Adapt and Upgrade: Increase your character's statistics through daily activities. Higher stats unlock unique, specialized escape routes that wouldn't be possible otherwise.

  • Stay Under the Radar: The guards are always watching. Sneak around restricted areas, hide your contraband, and make sure you never get caught.

Freedom is sweeter when shared—but survival is personal. In every match, you face a critical choice: work as a unified team or look out only for yourself.

You can pool your resources, share valuable information about guard patrols, and coordinate a massive group breakout where everyone makes it out alive. Alternatively, you can use your friends as a distraction, keep the best escape routes to yourself, and turn the match into a cutthroat race to see who can taste freedom first.

Will you rise together as a legendary crew, or will you leave your inmates rotting in their cells?

Survival behind bars requires more than just raw materials—it takes the right skills to turn junk into tools of escape. Our deep crafting system is directly tied to your character's progression.

To unlock advanced blueprints and utilize specific items, you must actively train your character's attributes. Boost your Intelligence to decipher complex security systems and craft high-tech tools, or build up your Strength to forge heavy-duty equipment and handle makeshift weapons.

Every item you craft can change the course of the game. Create essential gear to carve out your route to freedom, or engineer traps and weapons to neutralize guards, subdue rival inmates, or sabotage your own friends' escape plans just to get ahead.

To avoid throwing up red flags, you must blend in and live the life of a model prisoner—at least on the surface. A core part of your survival means keeping up with the daily prison grind and clocking in for your assigned shifts.

The facility offers a variety of prison jobs, each located in distinct sectors:

  • License Plate Pressing: Put your back into hard labor.

  • Dishwashing & Laundry: Keep the facility running smoothly.

  • Tailoring: Sew uniforms right under the guards' noses.

Working these jobs isn't just about passing the time; it’s a critical part of your strategy. These workplaces are prime locations to scavenge and smuggle out restricted items essential for your breakout.

Furthermore, the hard-earned money you make from your shifts can be put to good use. Spend your cash to buy valuable insider information from shady sources, or use it during your precious free time in the cafeteria to customize your character and elevate your gameplay experience.

The guards are always on high alert, and one wrong move can ruin days of careful planning. In this prison, boundaries are strictly enforced.

You must constantly monitor your surroundings and watch which doors you attempt to open. Stepping into a restricted zone or getting caught in the wrong place at the wrong time will trigger an immediate lockdown.

If you get caught by the guards, the consequences are severe: you will be thrown into solitary confinement, and every piece of contraband and valuable resource you’ve painstakingly gathered and crafted so far will be confiscated. Stay sharp, move in the shadows, and make sure your ultimate escape plan doesn’t end in total loss.

Whether you prefer a solo heist or a chaotic group breakout, the game adapts to your playstyle. Choose how you want to experience your sentence:

  • Singleplayer: Rely entirely on your own wits, skills, and stealth to outsmart the system.

  • Local Splitscreen: Share the couch and plan your escape side-by-side with a friend in classic split-screen action.

  • Online Co-op (Up to 6 Players): Host a lobby and bring in your entire crew for a massive, coordinated prison break.

To fully immerse you in the tension of the prison environment, the online experience features In-Game Voice Chat. Strategize in real-time, whisper plans in the corridors, or shout warnings when a guard approaches—providing the ultimate, authentic atmosphere of a real prison break.

[Synopsis]

Living in an isolated freezing village, you are a hated woodcutter whose only emotional support is your wife and son. One day, during a "Werewolf Trial," you are framed for all crimes by a malicious conspiracy.

Execution is set for tomorrow morning.

If you do nothing, your beloved family will be slaughtered as accomplices. To let them escape, you choose to become the scapegoat, burning at the stake as the unloved "Werewolf". —But after death, a horrific scene unfolds before your spirit. You witness your surviving family become toys for the mastermind, hopelessly broken.

"I... I have to save them...!" Your overwhelming regret warps time itself, and you wake up again in the prison on the eve of execution. Beside you, the ghost of a medium watches and sneers. The ultimate choice.

A blood-stained loop. Can you find the true path to let your loved ones escape safely, even if it means sacrificing yourself?

[Features]

🔪 Cruel Multiple Endings through "Death Loops" Your choices branch the story into pure despair. Distance your family by dying hated, or plead the truth only to drive your son to massacre the village. Every choice matters.

🐺 A Death Game of "Self-Sacrifice" This is not a game about reasoning out the culprit. It's a new type of despair visual novel where you must figure out how to be correctly executed as the "culprit" while letting your family escape.

🩸 The "Truth" Beyond Despair Through repeated loops, the village's madness and the terrifying truth hidden within "yourself" will be revealed. What decision will you make for love?

"Even if the whole world hates you, as long as your beloved family is smiling"

Streaming & Video Policy

You are free to stream, record, and monetize this game.

No permission needed. No need to contact us. No restricted sections.

We ask for one thing only.

Please keep the truth route — and what it reveals — out of your thumbnails and titles.

Viewers choose what they watch. Nobody chooses what shows up in their feed.

This game was written for the moment a single fact turns over.

One line in a thumbnail is enough to end that moment for someone who hasn't played yet.

Inside the video, spoil as much as you like.

Official thumbnail assets are available for streamers.

About the translation

This is a one-person project, so every language other than Japanese was translated with the help of AI. I wrote a glossary and check consistency automatically, but no native speaker has proofread the text. If something reads wrong, tell me and I will fix it.

Three Kingdoms Classic: Korea

Choose Where to Fight—And When to Negotiate

Move armies between strongholds by land and sea. Reinforce a threatened border, protect a key route, or reach a crossroads before the enemy does.

War is not your only option. Improve relations, seek a truce, or fight alongside an ally. Time gained through diplomacy can help you rebuild your forces, while a commitment on one front may leave another exposed.

Command Field Battles and Sieges Yourself

When armies meet, take direct control of infantry, archers, and cavalry in real-time battles. Plains, forests, rivers, and coasts create different approaches and risks. Adapt your formations to the ground and choose the moment to attack.

The tactics available change with the battlefield. Breach a dam to unleash a flood at supported crossings, hide troops in forests for an ambush, or trigger rockfalls on hilly ground. Fire attacks can disrupt an approach, but weather and the position of your own troops matter too.

In a siege, walls, gates, and access routes shape the fight. Position your troops to break through or hold the defenses. Victories and losses carry back to your armies and front lines on the campaign map.

One War, Decisions That Carry Forward

Capturing a stronghold is not the end of a campaign. Rebuild your armies, restore your provisions, and prepare for the next threat. Today's offensive may make tomorrow's defense harder.

Govern the kingdom, move the front, and lead the battle. The fate of the three kingdoms rests not on one victory, but on the choices that let you keep fighting.

This game is inspired by history. Battlefield layouts, character abilities, troop numbers, tactics, and diplomacy include adaptations and fictional elements for gameplay. The course and outcome of the war may differ from historical events depending on the player's choices.

Rule a house in 196 AD


Three Kingdoms Reimagined is a strategy game for one or two players. You rule from a pausable real-time campaign map of Han China and fight your battles yourself, with thousands of soldiers on the field. When you want to be in the fighting, press C: the camera sweeps down behind your general and you fight on in their place. Begin as Cao Cao, Liu Bei, Lu Bu, Sun Ce or another historical ruler, or create your own: choose a face, dress and arm them for battle, pick how they fight, and bring up to two companions you made.

Fight as your general


The Warrior view works in any single-player field battle, including sieges, passes, camps, villages and final stands, as long as your general is alive. Press C to fight in third person and C again to return to command. Your general has a four-hit light chain, a heavy blow off each light, a charged heavy, a dash strike and a parry. Fill the gauge and every weapon style has its own Musou: a call, a flurry of strikes and a finisher.

Duels where the blades meet


When two officers meet between the lines, one can challenge the other. Accept, and the ranks fall back to make a ring while the battle goes on around it. Before a battle you can call out the enemy commander, and that duel, like a tournament bout, you can fight yourself in the Warrior view. Every duel opens with an intro that builds each fighter's name across the screen.

When the blades lock, a clash begins. Mash to win the lock, then answer the prompts as the trades and blocks come. Get more than half of them right and the finisher is yours. Each weapon has its own signature moves. Against an archer the clash is a barrage of arrows to swat aside or dodge, and riders fight it out in passes, their blades meeting as they come level.



Command the battle


When armies meet, read the contact report first. It shows both forces and the stratagems you can afford: dust dragged behind your riders so the enemy thinks you are many, a bandit chief's horsemen waiting off their flank for your signal. The enemy plans its own. Then fight the battle yourself or let Auto Resolve settle it.

On the field, order your cohorts to move, attack or hold, and watch morale and fatigue before you commit them. Every company carries a standard marked with its type, and the flag shakes when the company wavers. Officers lead their own share of the army, and soldiers near an officer's banner hold together. Famous officers have moments of their own: Zhang Fei roars, Lu Bu breaks the first rank, Zhao Yun cuts his way out when he is surrounded. When your men break and run, raise a standard and rally them.

Fields are farm country, river crossings, steppe ridges, mountain valleys and terraced basins, each with its own roads, woods and villages.

Take the walls, or hold them


Cities are fought for on their own walls. Send a ram to the gate and ladder parties up the wall, and set your archers to keep the defenders' heads down. The garrison answers with boiling oil on the ram and stones on the ladders, and it will not break while its walls stand. Gate forts hold the passes between regions. In a single-player campaign, when an enemy storms a town your army is in, you can man the battlements yourself.

The Champions' Tournament


Once in a campaign, Lu Bu calls the strongest houses to a tournament at his parade ground. If he has fallen, the strongest house hosts. Each house sends its best fighter. Choose your champion, fight each bout yourself in the arena or let it resolve, and watch the others. Every house that enters is paid by how far its champion went, and the winner gains +3 WAR for good and the title Champion of the Realm.

Keep a court


Your officers come to you when something happens. After a deed, a wound, or a plan you set aside, an officer's card waits on the map with one line and two answers, and the campaign keeps running while you decide. They ask for what matters to them: a command, a duel with a named enemy, an office. Promise it and the promise has a deadline. Keep it and they owe you a favor; break it and everyone who values good faith hears.

Your choices build your name: merciful or severe, bold or cautious, faithful or faithless. Officers make friends in battle and rivals over honors. Swear an oath with a trusted officer once you have faced danger together, marry, or arrange a match between two of your court. The Bonds screen shows one officer at the centre with the ties around him. Sworn brothers, spouses and friends steady each other's men when they fight side by side, and when one falls, the other may rage or falter.

The Annals


After the first months, dated crises reach your court. A pretender claims the throne, Lu Bu is cornered at Xiapi, and the north fights its great war. Each crisis gives you ten days and several answers, and at least one leads to a grand battle you can fight yourself. Turning Points such as a captive emperor, a general who changes banners and a last coalition arrive one at a time.

If you take a stranger's dirty work, a darker road opens: bandit pacts, black-sealed letters and officers taken by force. Fear brings in tribute and cheap levies, and it breeds conspiracies at court. A player who never takes the first job sees none of it.

A map of the Han realm


The campaign map is laid out on real longitude and latitude, with the rivers, lakes and mountain ranges of Han China. Roads run from capital to capital through the towns between and the gates that hold the passes. Develop settlements, muster troops, trade grain and goods, and appoint officers to lead armies or run your cities. Your council proposes plans; you choose which one your commanders follow. Scouts and reports show part of the situation, not every enemy movement.



Make peace by sending an envoy with terms, gold or a returned captive, or bind another court to yours by marriage. A beaten enemy army falls back to a friendly city to recover. Hold 20 of the realm's 38 capitals to claim the Mandate, and expect the other courts to unite against you before the end. Win as Emperor, as Regent of the Han or as King, depending on the road you took. Lose your last holding and your house falls.

Every battle carries on


A victory may win territory while leaving your army too weak to press on. Survivors, wounds, captured officers and lost gates all stay in the campaign. Officers earn deeds, traits and titles, teach each other on campaign, and remember the promises you kept. A commander who keeps beating one of yours becomes a nemesis. Each officer's biography and your campaign's Chronicle keep the story.

Share the campaign with a friend


Two players can play one campaign together, each leading a historical warlord from their own seat. Begin as allies, at peace or at war, and keep the alliance or break it. Allies fight in each other's battles, each commanding their own army; rivals race each other for the realm. Each player can bring a character they created as a champion in their army. Stop and save together and carry on later. Custom Battle has a multiplayer lobby too, with drafted officers and armies of up to 500 men. The Warrior view and duel intros are single-player only.

Also in this build


  • English and Simplified Chinese
  • Steam achievements
  • Gamepad play
  • Steam Cloud saves
  • Low, Balanced and High graphics presets

Screenshots and GIFs are captured from the current Early Access build. Some battles were set up for the camera.

In Three Kingdoms Story, choose your faction and build an army capable of unifying the realm.

  • Roll the dice and move across the map

  • Recruit new officers and hire troops

  • Encounter events along the way

  • Claim key territories from rival factions

  • Pay to pass, or fight to take control

Your officers command their own troops and grow through battle, with different combinations creating unique synergies.

Battles play out in real time. Direct your units with formations and tactical commands as the fight unfolds.

Capture the final stronghold to complete the story, then carry your progress into the next.

Three Kingdoms: March is a tactical strategy simulation set in the age of the Three Kingdoms. Become a ruler in a time of war, command your armies in battle, and grow your realm through officers, policies, and research.

In battle, you directly command units by dragging orders across the field. Victory is not decided by numbers alone. Strike the enemy's flanks and rear, use fire tactics, encirclement, and breakthroughs, and turn the tide with careful battlefield judgment.

On the world map, you manage cities, appoint officers, develop technology, and strengthen your realm. Choosing who to assign, what to improve, and when to prepare for war can change the course of your campaign.

Key Features

- Real-time tactical battles controlled with drag-based commands

- Large-scale unit warfare built around flanks, rear attacks, encirclement, and breakthroughs

- A Three Kingdoms campaign centered on famous factions and officers

- Realm management through policies, research, and officer assignments

- A deep single-player strategy simulation

Content included in the base game

  • Includes the scenario content of “Up to Red Cliffs” and “To Unification”.
  • Scenarios and world-conquest content unlock as you progress through the game.
  • Supports 45 Steam achievements and Steam Cloud saves.

Optional add-on: Skins & Custom Officers

Skins & Custom Officers is a separately sold DLC that adds portrait skins for existing officers, custom officer creation, and the ability to start your own faction. Requires Three Kingdoms: March. Download and install the additional content through Steam before using these features.

Throneforged

Throneforged is a competitive 4X turn-based strategy game built for players who demand mastery over luck. Raise armies, research ancient technologies, seize multi-hex fortresses, and crush your rivals — all without a single dice roll. If you win, it's because you outplayed.

Command Six Asymmetric Factions

Begin as a neutral empire with a shared roster of warriors, archers, cavalry, scouts, and siege engines. As you advance into a new era of technology, your empire finds its identity — and you choose your destiny.

  • Solari Dominion — A versatile human empire whose veteran units hit the field faster than anyone else. Their Battlemage combines melee resilience with solar arcane fire.

  • Thornwood Covenant — Elven wardens who plant and reshape forests, turning the terrain itself into an impenetrable fortress. Their ancient Treants are the wall that never breaks.

  • Ironhold Clans — Dwarven engineers who fortify at half-cost and march through mountains. Their Runesmiths curse enemy units, turning the foe's own defenses against them.

  • Ashen Horde — Orcish raiders who move faster, hit harder, and burn everything. Their Warg Riders chain kills into free repositioning, striking and vanishing before you can react.

  • Tidecallers — Mages who flood the battlefield, dominate open water, and drag land units into the deep with their colossal Leviathan.

  • Umbral Pact — Undead attritionists who grow stronger as the body count rises. Their Lich harvests souls from every kill on the board, then raises entire graveyards as skeleton armies.

Every faction has a Tier 2 unit that replaces and upgrades your early forces, and a devastating Tier 4 elite that defines the late game. Faction choice is permanent — but deferred. You won't commit until mid-game, when the board state demands it.

The Throne Awaits — But So Does Its Guardian

At the heart of every map stands the Central Keep — seven hexes of ancient stone guarded by Thornwrath the Eternal, a colossal siege guardian fused to the walls over centuries. Before anyone can claim the Keep, Thornwrath must fall. His Warden's Aura fires the Keep's cannons automatically. His Rampart Slam hurls anyone who gets too close. His Unyielding passive means no single strike can kill him — the finishing blow must come separately.

Four Outposts ring the Keep, each sealed by Vorruk the Ironbound — a mercenary warlord who erupts from behind the walls the moment they fall. These are one-time encounters. Once a guardian falls, they stay fallen.

Deterministic Combat. No Exceptions.

Throneforged contains zero random number generation in gameplay. Damage values are calculated, not rolled. Combat outcomes can always be predicted. The only randomness is the procedurally generated map — mirrored for competitive fairness and seed-reproducible for tournament replay.

What this means: every hex you stand on matters. Every flanking angle you exploit is a real edge. Every unit you let die is a real mistake.

Deepen Your Army With XP, Gear, and Abilities

Units are characters. They gain experience through combat and passive service, promoting through Recruit, Veteran, Elite, and Champion tiers. Promotion unlocks powerful abilities:

  • Veterans gain Primary Abilities (Shield Wall, Radiant Charge, Tidal Surge, Life Drain...)

  • Champions unlock devastating Ultimates (Rain of Arrows, Stampede, Army of the Dead, Tsunami...)

Gear drops from cleared monster camps — predetermined, never random. Scouting a camp reveals its loot before you fight. A Tier 3 item might be worth the engagement cost. It might not.  Items level as well just as units do.

Monster Camps, Creeps, and Boss Encounters

Monster camps dot the map with escalating threats: Stone Sentinels, Direwolves, Wind Serpents, Ogre Chieftains, and four Boss-tier creatures — the Dragon, Stone Golem, Arcane Elemental, and Mana Serpent. Defeat them for team buffs and guaranteed loot. Cleared camps respawn as the next tier up. Boss camps don't respawn at all.

A Strategic Layer That Rewards Long-Term Thinking

  • Technology Trees span five Eras, from Foundations through Ascension. Research gates unit production, unlocks buildings, opens harvesting, and eventually grants faction-exclusive late-game powers.

  • Cities grow through population, supported by Farm clusters. At Level 5 they can construct a Faction Mega-Building — the Solari Sun Spire, the Forgeheart Citadel, the Bloodmoon Pyre, and more.

  • Resource Harvesting rewards map control. Claim plains for Crops and Animals. Resources respawn as long as a building is not placed on the hex. Sail to open water for Fish. Control the central corridors and your star economy accelerates.

  • Supply Caravans ferry resources from camps to your Keep and Outposts. Intercept your opponent's and deny theirs.

  • Naval Warfare opens with Sailing tech — Galleys, War Galleys, Dreadnoughts, and the kamikaze Fire Ship unlock a full second front.

The Snake Turn System

Initiative alternates every five turns, with the trailing player receiving a double-turn at each transition. No permanent first-player advantage. No coin flip. The tempo of the game shifts, and so must your strategy.

Competitive at Its Core

Built for players who want a skill ceiling, not a slot machine:

  • Zero RNG in all combat and production

  • Mirror-symmetric maps with seed-based generation for tournament integrity

  • Ranked matchmaking, replays, and tournament support (roadmap)

  • One Victory Condition in Multiplayer: Keep Supremacy - Control the Central Keep for 10 turns.

  • Single Player 50 turn limit: Total Score tallied and ranked on a leaderboard.

Features

  • Incredibly in depth combat formula that incorporates the day/night cycle, terrain modifiers, controlled territory modifiers, item modifiers, tech tree modifiers, and more.

  • 4X turn-based strategy on a procedurally generated hex grid

  • 6 asymmetric factions with unique units, passives, and Mega-Buildings

  • Deterministic combat — zero RNG in gameplay

  • Full tech tree spanning 5 eras with faction-exclusive late-game branches

  • RPG-style unit progression: XP, promotions, gear, and abilities

  • Named boss encounters guarding map objectives

  • Naval warfare with 4 ship types

  • Day/Night cycle affecting Lawful and Chaotic unit performance

  • Terrain system with 12 tile types, forest clearing, and resource harvesting

  • Mirror-symmetric maps, seed-reproducible for tournament play

  • Online Multiplayer

A fallen kingdom, breached walls, and a single warrior remaining to protect the throne at the center of the arena... **Throneguard: Last Stand** is a 3D medieval action tower defense game that blends fast-paced sword combat with strategic defense mechanics.

Enemy hordes don't follow a set corridor—they spawn at random locations across the map, converging on the castle at the center from every direction. As the castle's final guardian, you must face this 360-degree threat by personally fighting on the front lines with your sword while building defensive perimeters around the throne.

## ⚔️ KEY FEATURES

* **360-Degree Perimeter Defense:** Enemies don't stick to fixed paths! Adapt to waves spawning randomly across the arena and protect every side of your central fortress.

* **Action Meets Strategy:** Don't just build towers and watch! Take direct control of your hero, slash through enemy ranks with your sword, and fight alongside your defense lines.

* **Freeform Construction & Preparation Phase:** Make the most of the time between enemy waves. Build barricades and defense towers around the central throne to block, delay, and dismantle incoming attacks.

* **Hero Progression & Leveling System:** Earn experience points (XP) in combat to level up your warrior. Upgrade your damage, health, and combat abilities to face tougher challenges in upcoming rounds.

* **Protect the Central Throne at All Costs:** Surrounded on all sides, the throne is the heart of the kingdom. Set your defenses, draw your blade, and fight to the very last breath!

[A Romantic Journey of Waiting and Echoes]

Hidden in a corner of this city, five girls carry their unique pasts.

Piece together glowing fragments of their lives via jigsaw puzzles,

from the soft glow of dawn, faint light of quiet hours, to whispers only shared with you.

This is not a fast-paced thrilling game.

It is a tranquil journey to slow down your pace and calm your heart.

Core Gameplay

• Puzzle-Driven Story: Clear a puzzle to unlock its chapter plot

• 20 Exquisite Stages: From first encounter to exclusive episodes, difficulty rises gradually

• Every puzzle holds a complete story — not just art, but precious memories

Five Girls, Five Hearts

Aoi

"Make every ordinary day shine bright."

Nagi

"I want to become someone others can rely on."

Yume

"Live every single day in sweet bliss."

Natsuki

"I hope someone can stay by my side and share every joy of progress."

Rei

"Find my own warm little corner amid repetitive daily routines."

Game Features

• Elegant blend of jigsaw puzzles & narrative — gameplay and story complement each other

• Fully hand-drawn art style — every illustration carries a piece of the tale

• Perfect for casual play: short stages support pause anytime, ideal for commutes & bedtime

• Easy to pick up for all ages; veteran puzzle fans will find satisfying challenges in 6×12 layouts

About This Game

This is your laid-back romantic escape.

No nagging NPCs, no rush timers pushing you to hurry.

Only you, a puzzle, and a girl who’s been waiting for you.

Grab a puzzle piece. She’s waited far too long.

Tianyan Jie: Relics of Qiankun is an action roguelike set in a dark, ink-wash wuxia world—where every brushstroke of mist hides another blade.

Choose your martial sect and step into the heavenly tribulation. Fight through linked rooms, claim rewards, and weave secret manuals and legendary Qiankun relics into a build that is uniquely yours. Chain melee attacks, crowd-control enemies, and turn each run into a fresh path through the jianghu.

Features

  • Wuxia action roguelike — room-to-room runs with roguelike rewards and build variety

  • Ink-wash visual style — moody teal-grey palettes, volumetric fog, and cinematic wuxia atmosphere

  • Deep in-run builds — secret manuals, Jianghu relics, martial arts, and meridian growth

  • Satisfying melee combat — combo chains and fight-many-at-once action

  • Single-player focused — learn patterns, stack your build, push further each run

Coming Soon

A satisfying incremental game where crossing items off your to-do list powers your progression. Dive into a desktop full of checklists, optimize your daily workflow, and watch your earnings take off as you climb the corporate ladder and eventually become the CEO.

Chain Massive Combos!

Race against the clock to finish as many tasks as you can before the "day" ends. When the timer hits zero, cash out in a satisfying results screen where multipliers and combos send your numbers flying.

Play Your Way!

Every task provides different boosts and rewards. You choose the order and which assignments to prioritize, allowing you to adjust your progression to your specific playstyle and strategy.

Automate the Bureaucracy!

Unlock and assign Interns to automate tasks in the background.
